what: AppLovin runs an advertising platform. Its Axon system decides which ad to show to which person inside mobile apps, and it is paid when advertisers hit their return targets. It has sold off most of its own games business to focus on advertising.
customers: App developers and, increasingly, e-commerce and consumer brands buying advertising; app publishers who sell space through it.
money: the Axon engine matching advertisers with audiences inside apps
moat: A self-improving machine-learning engine trained on enormous volumes of ad outcomes, plus direct links into many mobile apps that competitors do not have.
risks: Growth has come from a single advertising engine, so a step down in its performance hits everything
Advertising budgets fall quickly in a downturn
Apple and Google control the platforms it depends on and change privacy rules
Short-seller reports have questioned its measurement and growth claims
opportunities: Moving beyond mobile games into e-commerce advertising opens a much larger pool of spending
Operating margins above 70% mean most new revenue drops to profit
Strong cash generation funds continuous share buybacks
watch: Whether revenue from non-gaming advertisers keeps growing, and the pace of buybacks.
